QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_29

question.text: In an SIA engagement, 'materiality' governs which outcomes the SIA focuses assurance procedures on. The BEST definition is:

answer.text: Outcomes whose omission or misstatement could influence the decisions of the AIR's intended users
Outcomes whose monetary value exceeds 2% of CSR spend
Outcomes that received media coverage in the reporting year
Outcomes the SE's board voted to include in the AIR

explanation.text: The Logic: Materiality in assurance is defined in terms of the user of the report: outcomes whose omission or misstatement could reasonably be expected to influence the decisions of the AIR's intended users (donors, SSE investors, SEBI, regulators). It is qualitative + quantitative, not purely monetary. The Trap: The 2% CSR rule is a Sec 135 spend threshold, not materiality. Media coverage is not a materiality test. Board vote is governance, not assurance materiality. Cross-Exam Context: III-A / III-C Compliance and XV Research Analyst use financial-audit materiality. XXIII adapts the concept to impact outcomes. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Document materiality in two axes: (1) size — number of beneficiaries or monetised outcome value; (2) significance — depth of outcome (life-saving > nice-to-have). Weight both in your scoping memo.
